1  Precipitation

1.1 Overall Summary

2025 was normal-to-dry across the Mississippi Sound Watershed. In terms of the annual total precipitation received, about 1/3 of the subbasins were within 5% of the 30-year average total. The others ranged about 10-20% lower for their annual totals. The subbasins that were driest were generally in the southern portions of the watershed, whereas the more northern subbasins were closer to the long-term average. See Figure 1.1 and Figure 1.3 in particular for details.

In terms of monthly totals, May was a little bit wet, particularly in the middle portion of the watershed, and the dry months were September and November. See Figure 1.7.

For a summary table of annual and monthly totals, normals, and % difference from normal, see Table 1.1.

1.2 Supporting Information

1.2.1 Annual Precipitation, Averaged to HUC8

Annual totals were calculated from monthly precipitation data obtained from the PRISM Group at Oregon State University, https://prism.oregonstate.edu which were accessed 29 July 2026.

1.2.2 Monthly Precipitation

Monthly data are from the PRISM Group at Oregon State University, https://prism.oregonstate.edu and were accessed 29 July 2026. They are again averaged to HUC8. Monthly normals are also from the PRISM group, and were compiled in the msepBaselineData R package.

1.2.2.1 Monthly Anomalies

From long-term climate normals, as provided by the PRISM Climate Group at Oregon State University and processed into the msepBaselineData package’s precip_normals_huc8avg dataset.
